verification.note: Fresh selected primary reading381–383,386–391,394–395,399–407, including corresponding endnotes;389,391and400also visually collated from renderedPDFpages. sources.title: Michael Katz’s Contribution to Social and Social Welfare History
sources.citation: Mark J.Stern, “Michael Katz’s Contribution to Social and Social Welfare History,” Social Science History41(4),Winter2017,768–771,doi10.1017/ssh.2017.32; in combined2015SSHA memorial-session PDF.

verification.note: Fresh selected reading of Stern’s complete768–771tribute in the deposited combined23-pagePDF. Stern differentiates the Hamilton collaborative family-economy work, Chayanov’s work/consumption index, early structure emphasis and later moral/agency voice. He names Doucet and his own joint credit, SusanDavis’s Brooklyn discovery and the Ravitch criticism; these have no full individual graph endpoints. Other contributions in the combinedPDF were read selectively only; Graff’s opening757–759also distinguishes intellectual mentoring from lone-scholar production. No original book body newly read;2015session and2017publication distinct.

hc175_michael_b_katz_2.note: Fresh selected rereading2026-10-28: Thomas Sugrue’s own memorial, reproduced by PennPress25August2014, paragraphs beginning with first meeting during dissertation work and reading The Undeserving Poor on a plane. Explicit support, intellectual affinity and guidance support a scoped mentorship relationship. Publisher/editorial memorial and Sugrue’s recollection remain distinct. The memorial dates that book1988; a later Stern scholarly retrospective gives1989, so no first-publication year is inferred from the recollection.
